patch.value: CLI argv keeps one value silently when two spellings of one extension flag differ (--status-filter a -s b), while direct callers are refused with extension_option_spelling_conflict

Found by CodeRabbit on PR 1682 (pm-gh1665). The shared extension option normalizer now refuses two spellings of one declared flag with different values for PmClient.run, MCP and the test harness (extension_option_spelling_conflict). CLI argv dispatch still folds them through mergeAliasOptionKeys in src/sdk/extension/command-options.ts: for scalar flags the canonical value wins and the alias value is dropped without a refusal, so pm demo --status-filter open -s closed silently runs with open. The parse-time occurrences recorded by parseLooseCommandOptions carry enough information to apply the same conflict check before dispatch. Changing this alters CLI behavior for existing scripts that repeat a flag under two spellings, so it was deferred from the batch. Duplicate check: searched spelling conflict, alias folding, repeated flag values and short alias across all statuses; pm-kfq5 owns list accumulation across long/short occurrences, not scalar conflicts.

CLI argv that supplies two spellings of one declared scalar extension flag with different values exits 2 with extension_option_spelling_conflict naming both spellings and the handler key; Equal values and list flags keep their current accumulation; A spec drives the built CLI with --long and -s spellings, with a negative control that restores silent folding
Declare --status-filter with short -s, run pm demo --status-filter open -s closed --json
exit 0; the handler receives statusFilter open
